subject: Pilot gating checklist and owner commitments — Redwood / CareFirst MAP
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@carefirst.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot gating checklist and owner commitments — Redwood / CareFirst MAP

Hi Daniel — great conversation this morning. Quick recap + proposed owners for the MAP technical milestone (pilot / evaluation gating). Please confirm that this matches what we agreed and flag anything missing.

High-level target
- Pilot goal: validate inference quality and unit economics for a single CareFirst workflow (member claim triage)
- Target close for this MAP milestone: 2027-04-30 (pilot validation complete)

Proposed gating checklist (success criteria):
1) Functional: end-to-end integration with CareFirst sandbox API and request/response fidelity (pass/fail) — owner: CareFirst IT / Redwood integration (Ben)
2) Quality: automated evals show no more than 5% drop vs baseline on intent classification + qualitative signoff from the product team — owner: CareFirst product (Daniel) and Redwood evals (Rishi)
3) Latency: p95 <= 450ms for 256-token average across peak 50 RPS test window — owner: Redwood infra (Rishi)
4) Cost: token cost target <= $0.0025 per generated token (after batching/quantization), with a plan to get to $0.0018 within next quarter — owner: Redwood commercial (Ben)
5) Reliability: end-to-end SLO 99.5% for the pilot window; automated fallback to smaller model on degradation — owner: Redwood infra (Rishi)

Dependencies and blockers
- CareFirst to provide sandbox API keys and a representative dataset by 2027-04-05 (dependency: CareFirst IT)
- Completion of security questionnaire (attached) and confirmation of data retention policy — required before on-prem/private trial
- Redwood to provision dedicated pilot pool (GPU allocation) and share runbook — target 2027-04-08 (owner: Ben / Rishi)

Next steps / action items
- Daniel: confirm sandbox access ETA and product stakeholder for qualitative signoff (reply)
- Ben: prepare pilot cost estimate + runbook and share by 2027-04-02
- Rishi: draft benchmark script and measurement plan; post initial draft to Drive by 2027-04-01

Attachments: carefirst-security-questionnaire.pdf (stub), pilot-benchmark-specs.xlsx (stub)

Thanks — I’ll update the MAP doc after we confirm dates.

Evelyn Hart
Account Director, Redwood Inference

Evelyn — thanks for the recap. Looks good overall. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Sandbox ETA: our API team expects to hand over sandbox credentials by 2027-04-04 (slight delay vs 4/5) — I can escalate if needed.
- Product owner for qualitative signoff: Sarah Lee (cc'd to this reply would be ideal, I can loop her in once we confirm the test plan).
- The security questionnaire is mostly complete; I attached notes in-line in the doc we received. We can share the final PDF by 2027-04-03.

One ask: during the pilot we'll need an agreed sample set for the automated evals (approx. 1,200 cases). Can Redwood share an initial proposal for the selection criteria?

I'll confirm Sarah and sandbox keys by Friday.

— Daniel

daniel@carefirst.com

Subject: Re: Pilot gating checklist and owner commitments — Redwood / CareFirst MAP

Thanks Daniel — noted on the sandbox ETA. Quick responses and commitments from Redwood: 

- Pilot cost estimate & runbook: I will produce an initial estimate (GPU hours, expected token throughput, burst strategy) and a concise runbook with cutover/fallback steps by 2027-04-02.
- Sample selection criteria for evals: draft attached in pilot-benchmark-specs.xlsx — short summary below:
  * 1,200 cases sampled from recent anonymized production logs, stratified by intent and error category
  * 70/30 split automated vs hand-labeled (hand labels for high-sensitivity cases)
  * Benchmarks: intent F1 >= baseline -5%, hallucination rate < 1.5% on targeted prompts

- Cost target: our starting config will run on a quantized 8-bit variant of the shortlisted model(s). If the initial numbers exceed $0.0025/token, we will present two cost-reduction levers: 1) increased batching, 2) fallback smaller model for low-risk intents.

I'll upload the runbook and a one-page executive summary to the Drive folder by EOD 2027-04-02.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Thanks — a few technical clarifications and proposed metric definitions I want on record before we finalize the MAP doc: 

1) Latency measurement: p95 <= 450ms measured over a 50-RPS synthetic replay using the production-shaped request-size distribution. We will run three 30-minute windows during the pilot (baseline, after quantization, after batching).
2) Cost measurement: token-cost is defined as net infra + model execution spend divided by generated tokens in the measurement window; we will include a sensitivity table in the benchmark sheet showing cost at 25/50/75 RPS.
3) Model shortlist (initial):
   - LlamaX-70B-q4 (primary candidate)
   - LlamaX-13B-q4 (fallback for lower-cost path)
   - RedSea-30B-int8 (experimental; better latency in some configs)
4) Eval scripts: I will push a first draft of the benchmark script to the Drive folder (link above) by 2027-04-01. Please review and comment by 2027-04-05 so we can lock the test harness.

I also attached a quick checklist for our infra runbook (node types, expected KV cache sizing, monitoring hooks).

Rishi

Lead Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
